correctness.rationale: For μ,S,u,v>0, the stable 3x3 Lyapunov equation has a unique solution. The exact control determinant is p²(S²-4p)/[32μ(μ+S)²(4μ²+4μS+3p)²(μ²+2μS+3p)], obtained by exact Cauchy and Kalman determinant identities and independently reconstructed symbolically by solving nine Lyapunov equations. A quadratic Q in normalized p has positive leading coefficient and negative constant for every damping ratio, hence exactly one positive stationary root; F vanishes on each product-domain boundary and has a unique interior global maximum. The positive root is <1/6, monotone with damping, and its small/large damping expansions follow via nonsingular rescaled polynomial roots. Exact symbolic checker replayed successfully; finite root illustrations do not establish infinite parameter statements.

value.rationale: The exact object is the smallest star whose single hub control can be full rank, the objective is reachability ellipsoid volume, and a fixed total conductance is a natural physical design constraint. The theorem classifies all optimizers for every positive damping ratio, proves a counterintuitive asymmetric limit, and exhibits an optimized μ^{-2} versus any fixed distinct design μ^{-1} volume determinant law. That sharp asymptotic tradeoff is more than a textbook normalization or small numerical table; it provides a benchmark for topology-constrained control-network design.
